summary.text: Kambrell Garvin is a Democratic state representative from Richland County who has represented South Carolina House District 77 since November 2018 and is seeking re-election on November 3, 2026.
An attorney and former public school teacher, Garvin serves on the Education and Public Works and Government Efficiency and Legislative Oversight committees.

paragraphs.text: Garvin earned a B.A. from Winthrop University in 2013, where he was student government president and an ex-officio member of the Board of Trustees from 2011 to 2013.
He taught in the Colleton County School District from 2013 to 2016 as a Teach for America alumnus.

He later earned a master's degree in education from Johns Hopkins University in 2016, a J.D. from the University of South Carolina School of Law in 2019, and an M.B.A. from South Carolina State University in 2024.
Garvin is principal attorney and owner of the Kambrell Garvin Law Firm, LLC.
He took office in the House on November 12, 2018, succeeding Joseph McEachern.
He served as treasurer of the South Carolina House Democratic Caucus from 2022 to 2024 and has been co-chair of the Judicial Committee of the South Carolina Legislative Black Caucus since 2024.
